In this notebook I obtain the complexity variabilities of Boston and Monterrey. The complexity of a building's footprint is defined as the footprint perimeter divided by the footprint's area:

$$\text{Complexity} = \frac{\text{Perimeter}}{\text{Area}}$$

The units depend on the CRS that you use. We use `EPSG:4326`, which is the one utilized in other studies. 

The metric has more sensitivity than specificity. If a building has a complex shape that usually means it will have a higher perimeter and thus higher complexity. However, you can also get a high complexity if the building has a regular shape but it's very small. 

We measure the complexity variability as the interquartile range of complexity:

$$IQR_{\text{complexity}} = P_{75,\text{complexity}} - P_{25, \text{complexity}}$$

It's important to know that the variability here is computed over the normalized complexity.

```{python}
import json


PATH_DATA = "/Users/legariapena.j/Documents/imageable-2026/imageable/data/training_validation_data/data.json"

with open(PATH_DATA, "r") as f:
    data = json.load(f)

validation_data = [x for x in data if x["data_type"] == "validation"]

#Boston validation data
boston_validation = [x for x in validation_data if x["city"] == "Boston"]
#Monterrey validation data
monterrey_validation = [x for x in validation_data if x["city"] == "Monterrey"]

feature_names = data[0]["feature_names"]
COMPLEXITY_FEATURE_NAME = "complexity"
complexity_index = feature_names.index(COMPLEXITY_FEATURE_NAME)

import numpy as np
def assess_iqr(values):
    median = np.percentile(values, 50)
    p25 = np.percentile(values, 25)
    p75 = np.percentile(values, 75)
    return p75 - p25, median

feature_vectors_boston = [x["features"] for x in boston_validation]
feature_vectors_monterrey = [x["features"] for x in monterrey_validation]
#Get lists with the complexity values
complexity_values_boston = [x[complexity_index] for x in feature_vectors_boston]
complexity_values_monterrey = [x[complexity_index] for x in feature_vectors_monterrey]

range_boston, median_boston = assess_iqr(complexity_values_boston)
range_monterrey, median_monterrey = assess_iqr(complexity_values_monterrey)

print(f"The complexity variability in Boston is {range_boston}")
print(f"The complexity variability in Monterrey is {range_monterrey}")
```
